chunks.arabic_text: عُمَرُ بْنُ تَوْبَةَ، أَبُو يَحْيَى، الصَّنْعَانِيُّ. يَرْوِي عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Umar ibn Tawba, Abu Yahya, al-San'ani. He narrates from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

en.summary: This entry from *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights 'Umar ibn Tawba al-Ṣanʿānī, a narrator of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), whose classification as 'very weak' (da'if jiddan) indicates his narrations are generally not relied upon for establishing legal rulings. In Shia rijal scholarship, this level of weakness often implies significant issues with memory or precision, distinguishing him from those merely considered 'weak' but still acceptable in certain contexts. His specific mention underscores the rigorous scrutiny applied to the chain of transmission even from the Imams to ensure the authenticity of hadith literature.
en.seo_question: What is the status of 'Umar ibn Tawba in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ: Not turned to / not relied upon
